does: Sets beaten eggs into a thin, tender sheet with a creamy middle, and rolls it into a smooth, pale cylinder.
how: Heat butter in a pan over medium heat until it foams and the foam starts to fall.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir fast in small circles while shaking the pan.
Stop stirring when the eggs are mostly set but still wet on top, and let the bottom firm for a moment.
Scatter any filling down the middle.
Tilt the pan, fold the near edge over, and roll the omelette to the far lip.
Turn it out onto the plate, seam side down.

cues.text: A pale yellow, smooth skin with no brown. The top still glistens when you start to roll.
The omelette slides freely when the pan is shaken.

mistakes.mistake: The pan is too hot, so the skin browns and turns leathery.
mistakes.fix: Lift the pan off the heat while you stir, and turn the heat down.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting for the top to dry before rolling, which leaves the middle firm and dull.
mistakes.fix: Roll while the top is still wet. The heat inside finishes it.

comes_after.why: The first half of an omelette is a fast scramble. A cook who can stop a scramble in time can stop an omelette in time.
